text: The purpose of the monte di pieta (literally, â€œmountain of compassionâ€), or pawnshop was to provide small amounts of credit to anyone, even if poor, who was in a position to provide collateral with a value at least a third more than what was received.

The purpose of the monte di pieta 
(literally, â€œmountain of compassionâ€), or pawnshop was to 
provide small amounts of credit to anyone, even if poor, who 
was in a position to provide collateral with a value at least a

text: During the late Middle Ages, this institution moved into the credit the credit arena, which Christians and above all Jewish lenders previously dominated, by acquiring agreements, called condotte, from various Cities to provide credit at stipulated conditions.

During the late Middle

text: The Observant Friars Minor, a branch of the Franciscan order, assumed the task of promoting the first pawnshops, persuading the richest inhabitants and the civic authorities to offer the capital necessary for its operation.

order, assumed the task of promoting the first pawnshops,

text: A series of theoretical passages, from Pietro di Giovanni Olivi (1248-1298), a Franciscan philosopher and thelogian, to Bernardino da Siena (1380-1444) one of the most famous Franciscan preachers of the late Middle Ages, had led Ob- servant Franciscans to experiment with the pawnshop as a concrete economic action that encouraged social harmony.

text: 224 POPULATION POPULATION.
text_raw:
224 POPULATION 
POPULATION.

text: Population is any permanent group of individuals renewing itself through reproduction and mi- gration, structured in a continuous sequence of genera- tions, defined and identified by one or more dimensions of a geographic, political, juridical, ethnic, religious, or cul- tural nature.
text_raw:
Population is any permanent group of 
individuals renewing itself through reproduction and mi- 
gration, structured in a continuous sequence of genera- 
tions, defined and identified by one or more dimensions of 
a geographic, political, juridical, ethnic, religious, or cul- 
tural nature.

text: Renewal takes place through biological re- production or social reproduction, which occurs when a group or population gains (or loses) individuals through migration.
text_raw:
Renewal takes place through biological re- 
production or social reproduction, which occurs when a 
group or population gains (or loses) individuals through 
migration.

text: Theory distinguishes between closed and open populations: in the former renewal is only biological (births); in the latter renewal is both biological and social (migration).
text_raw:
Theory distinguishes between closed and open 
populations: in the former renewal is only biological 
(births); in the latter renewal is both biological and social 
(migration).

text: Any accidental, occasional, or temporary col- lection of individuals (the crowd in a stadium, vacationers on the beach, patients in a hospital) although representing a population in technical or statistical terms, is not nor- mally the object of study of history, demography, or genet- ics.
text_raw:
Any accidental, occasional, or temporary col- 
lection of individuals (the crowd in a stadium, vacationers 
on the beach, patients in a hospital) although representing 
a population in technical or statistical terms, is not nor- 
mally the object of study of history, demography, or genet- 
ics.

text: In most cases a population is defined by geographical referencesâ€”natural, political, or administrative bound- ariesâ€”but populations are also commonly defined on the basis of religion, language, ethnicity, or other characteris- tics dictated by convenience or necessity.
text_raw:
In most cases a population is defined by geographical 
referencesâ€”natural, political, or administrative bound- 
ariesâ€”but populations are also commonly defined on the 
basis of religion, language, ethnicity, or other characteris- 
tics dictated by convenience or necessity.

text: Most historical analyses refer to geographically defined populations, but in many cases subgroups are treated as populations (ur- ban and rural population; aristocracy and commoners; farmers and laborers; masters and slaves; members of dif- ferent religious affiliation; speakers of different languages or dialects; individuals belonging to different ethnic groups or castes) with distinctive behaviors in terms of nuptiality, fertility, mortality, or mobility.

Most historical 
analyses refer to geographically defined populations, but

ban and rural population; aristocracy and commoners; 
farmers and laborers; masters and slaves; members of dif-

text: Modern counts and censuses have been held regularly since the early nineteenth century (although their origins are much more remote) to assess the size and characteris- tics of a population.
text_raw:
Modern counts and censuses have been held regularly 
since the early nineteenth century (although their origins 
are much more remote) to assess the size and characteris-

text: In census practice, a distinction is made between de facto and de jure or resident population: the first relating to the individuals actually living and working in a given territory even if on a temporary basis, or who happen to be present for other reasons at the mo- ment of the count.
text_raw:
In census practice, a distinction is 
made between de facto and de jure or resident population: 
the first relating to the individuals actually living and 
working in a given territory even if on a temporary basis, 
or who happen to be present for other reasons at the mo- 
ment of the count.

text: The second term relates only to those who have a juridical residential entitlement in the same territory, even if they have emigrated or are usually absent.

The second term relates only to those 
who have a juridical residential entitlement in the same 
territory, even if they have emigrated or are usually absent.

text: Another distinction is between urban and rural popula- tion, identified with a variety of criteria, the simpler being the one assigning the characteristics of urban to the popu- lation living in incorporated townships or cities above a certain size, while labeling everything else rural.

Another distinction is between urban and rural popula-

the one assigning the characteristics of urban to the popu- 
lation living in incorporated townships or cities above a 
certain size, while labeling everything else rural.

text: A related distinction, between farm and nonfarm (or agricultural and nonagricultural) population is based on the source of the householdâ€™s income and livelihood or the nature of the prevailing occupation of its members.

text: Institutional popu- lation refers to individuals who do not normally live in households, such as soldiers in barracks, patients in hospi- tals, the indigent in charitable establishments, the reli- gious in convents and monasteries.

text: Merely instrumental and descriptive are other uses of the term population, indi- cating subsets of individuals with determined biodemo- graphic (sex, age) or social characteristics (marital status, working status), such as male or female population, mar- riageable population, working age population, and school age population.

text: Broadly speaking, analysis tries to understand the mechanisms that determine population change and its age structure (relative size of each age group).

age structure (relative size of each age group).

text: In any peri- od of time, absolute change is determined by the balance of births and deaths (natural growth) and by the balance of immigration and emigration; in relative terms, these flows are translated into rates, their algebraic sum being the rate of growth (birth rate =b; death rate =d; immigration and emigration rates i and e, respectively; the rate of growth r being equal to b â€”d +i â€”e).

Bolshevik movement in Russia.
